section_summary: This section documents SCAP’s authorization of a Japanese Antarctic whaling expedition for the 1946–47 season and the objections raised by Norway, Australia, New Zealand, and Britain. It includes directives, diplomatic discussions, proposed replies, and material on inspection, security, food supply, and whale oil allocation. The final pages contain Japanese charts of earlier Antarctic whale catches.

subfiles.title: Antarctic Whaling Directive and Staff Study: staff study
subfiles.from: Hubert G. Schenck, SCAP Natural Resources Section
subfiles.about: Recommends authorizing two Japanese factory ships and twelve killer boats for the 1946–47 Antarctic season.
subfiles.summary: The study cites shortages of whale oil and food, estimates the catch and products, and argues Japanese crews can operate the remaining vessels. It recommends a limited authorization under international rules and lists official concurrences.

subfiles.title: Japanese Whaling Operations in the Antarctic
subfiles.from: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: Authorizes a specified fleet to whale in a defined Antarctic area for one season.
subfiles.summary: SCAPIN 1103 names the factory ships, killer boats, and carriers, defines the operating area, and requires routing, position reports, catch reports, and whale oil storage notices. It requires observance of international whaling rules and says the authorization creates no precedent for later seasons or territorial claims.

subfiles.title: Whaling Industry
subfiles.from: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: Directs Japanese whaling to conform to international conventions and submit reports.
subfiles.summary: Requires convention compliance, carcass utilization, and marketing whale meat as food where possible.

subfiles.title: Japanese Antarctic Whaling
subfiles.about: Records Norway’s objection to the Japanese expedition and proposals to rescind it or use Norwegian crews.
subfiles.summary: The Norwegian representative said Norway had not been consulted and criticized Japan’s conservation record. He proposed reversing the authorization or placing the expedition under Norwegian operation; Acheson promised an inquiry.

subfiles.title: Whaling Industry
subfiles.from: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: Repeats the November 1945 directive governing Japanese whaling.
subfiles.summary: Duplicate copy requiring convention compliance, reports, full carcass use, and whale meat for food.

subfiles.title: Japanese Whaling Operations in Antarctic
subfiles.about: Records British Embassy concern and consultations with Commonwealth governments.
subfiles.summary: Graves reported wider British and Commonwealth interest and expected a government position by August 22.

subfiles.title: Japanese Whaling Operations in Antarctic
subfiles.about: Records Australia’s objections to Japanese whaling near its Antarctic interests.
subfiles.summary: Plimsoll raised security, lack of consultation, treaty quota, and precedent concerns. Australia preferred Allied operation of Japanese equipment and hoped to avoid a formal protest.

subfiles.title: Atcheson telegram on Ball’s whaling objection
subfiles.to: War Department and Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Reports correspondence with William MacMahon Ball and defends SCAP’s whaling authorization.
subfiles.summary: Atcheson describes Ball’s request to defer a final decision and MacArthur’s willingness to follow later Allied directives. He argues that the one-season expedition addresses food shortages, respects whaling rules, and prejudices no future rights.

subfiles.title: Japanese Whaling Question in Antarctic
subfiles.about: Reviews the authorization chronology and questions whether promised Allied consultations occurred.
subfiles.summary: Borton traces State, War Department, and SCAP messages from April through August. He notes uncertainty over treaty obligations and says he cannot determine whether consultations with other nations were begun.

subfiles.title: Atcheson telegram on Ball’s whaling objection
subfiles.about: Provides the State Department copy of Atcheson’s report on Ball’s objection.
subfiles.summary: Repeats the exchange with Ball and Atcheson’s defense of temporary Japanese whaling.

subfiles.title: Corrections to Atcheson telegram
subfiles.about: Supplies corrections to the received Atcheson telegram.
subfiles.summary: Correction copy for the August 22 telegram; OCR obscures most amended wording.

subfiles.title: Request to release SCAP whaling statement to Australian press
subfiles.from: H. Earle Russell, American Legation, Canberra
subfiles.about: Explains why the Legation declined to release a controversial SCAP statement to Australian newspapers.
subfiles.summary: Russell describes Australian press criticism of the whaling decision and the unfavorable reaction expected from External Affairs. Recalling earlier public disputes over the Yoizuki and Piet Hein, he seeks guidance for similar future requests.

subfiles.title: Atcheson request for Australian press release
subfiles.about: Requests publication of SCAP’s humanitarian explanation for temporary Japanese whaling.
subfiles.summary: Asks the Legation to give Australian newspapers a statement defending one-season whaling for Japan’s food supply.

subfiles.title: MacArthur statement on the Yoizuki incident
subfiles.from: United States Army in Australia on behalf of General MacArthur
subfiles.about: Assigns responsibility for loading the Yoizuki repatriation voyage to Australian forces.
subfiles.summary: The statement reproduces messages about transporting Formosan and Korean passengers. It says SCAP rejected requests to increase the ship’s load and ordered women and children transferred to the Hikawa Maru.

subfiles.title: Japanese Antarctic Whaling
subfiles.about: Lists questions requiring investigation before answering Allied objections.
subfiles.summary: Officials identify compliance inspections, catch quotas, Antarctic boundaries, Allied use of equipment, and Japan’s long-term whaling status as key issues. They agree to seek legal and geographic review.

subfiles.title: New Zealand objection to Japanese Antarctic whaling
subfiles.about: Protests the proposed expedition, citing proximity, conservation, security, and lack of consultation.
subfiles.summary: New Zealand objects and suggests that Allied operation of available Japanese vessels might address its concerns.

subfiles.title: Japanese Whaling in the Antarctic
subfiles.about: Records Colonel Powles’s presentation of New Zealand’s objection.
subfiles.summary: Powles raised security and policy concerns; Vincent sought fuller information from SCAP and a prompt response.

subfiles.title: Japanese Whaling in the Antarctic
subfiles.about: Restates the discussion with Powles, including Vincent’s preference for direct government talks.
subfiles.summary: Revised account adds Vincent’s wish to keep the issue on a government-to-government basis.

subfiles.title: United States reply to New Zealand on Antarctic whaling
subfiles.about: Defends the one-season expedition and describes inspection and security safeguards.
subfiles.summary: The reply grounds SCAP’s action in occupation authority and cites food and oil shortages. It promises observance of whaling rules, Allied inspectors, screening of Japanese personnel, route notification, and a twelve-mile distance from land. It says future whaling and the disposition of vessels require Allied consultation and asks New Zealand to withdraw its objection.

subfiles.title: Correction to the whaling expedition flag description
subfiles.about: Corrects the flag designation given in the October 4 aide-mémoire.
subfiles.summary: Specifies the SCAJAP “E” flag in place of the previously described “O” flag.

subfiles.title: Canberra report on Commonwealth whaling consultations
subfiles.about: Reports likely joint Commonwealth representations for Allied direction of the expedition.
subfiles.summary: Australia, New Zealand, and Britain were consulting; Russell also explains why the Legation withheld SCAP’s press statement.

subfiles.title: SCAP report on expanded Japanese fishing area
subfiles.about: Explains the food value of catches from an expanded Japanese fishing area.
subfiles.summary: SCAP estimates added monthly catches and describes fish as a vital source of animal protein.

subfiles.title: Charts of whale capture for Antarctic seasons 1935–41
subfiles.about: Forwards historical whale-capture charts.
subfiles.summary: Brief routing note transmitting charts of Antarctic catches.

subfiles.title: Forwarding letter and Japanese whaling charts
subfiles.about: Forwards a War Department letter and charts for action.
subfiles.summary: Sends Japanese Whaling Association charts and their covering letter.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of Antarctic whale-capture charts
subfiles.from: O. P. Echols, Civil Affairs Division
subfiles.about: Transmits Japanese charts showing whale-capture locations from 1935 to 1941.
subfiles.summary: Identifies the charts as supplemental information obtained from SCAP.

subfiles.title: Whale chart leaf
subfiles.about: A largely unreadable leaf associated with the transmitted whale charts.
subfiles.summary: Only a faint whaling label is legible in the OCR.

subfiles.title: Routing note on an attached telegram
subfiles.about: Redirects an attached telegram concerning oil to the division thought responsible.
subfiles.summary: Suggests the oil mentioned is vegetable oil and belongs with International Resources.

subfiles.title: Whaling Industry
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Encloses copies of SCAPIN 1154 on whaling regulations.
subfiles.summary: Cover despatch transmitting the August 24 SCAP directive.

subfiles.title: Whaling Industry: additional international protocols
subfiles.from: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: Adds later protocols to the international whaling rules binding Japanese operations.
subfiles.summary: SCAPIN 1154 supplements the 1945 directive with the 1944–46 protocols, lists the attached agreements, and requires notices and reports to SCAP.

subfiles.title: Japanese Antarctic whaling grounds and catch charts
subfiles.about: Maps historic whale catches across Antarctic waters and coastal sectors.
subfiles.summary: The title and foreword identify a Japanese Whaling Association compilation based on ships’ logs and official records. The visible pages contain a contents list and successive monthly charts, beginning with the 1935–36 season, marking catch locations and whale types around East Antarctica and the Ross Sea sector. The booklet continues beyond page 237.
